name: permission-wildcarding
description: Cuts agent approval friction, with a different mechanism per agent. Claude Code only: generalizes approved permissions into command-family wildcards on change, drains project-local approvals into user scope, and backs up policy before every write. Codex only: exports execpolicy prefix rules, validated by codex execpolicy check before anything is written. Shared: Auto Learn over both agents' history, a wildcardable shell style for the agent, memory gates, memory-index diagnostics, and prompt diagnostics. Codex has no wildcarding pass and no project-local promotion. Codex rule export is experimental.

permissionWildcarding.backupMirrorPath.markdownDescription: Where to mirror the allow/deny high-water-mark backup, in addition to `~/.claude/backups/allow-list.latest.json`. Empty uses `~/.permission-wildcarding/allow-list.latest.json`. The primary copy lives inside `~/.claude`, so it cannot survive that directory being recreated rather than merely rewritten — the mirror is the copy that can. Set it to a path on another volume to survive more than a reset. Written second and best-effort, so a bad path can never cost you the primary backup; restore reads the primary first and falls back to the mirror.

permissionWildcarding.autoLearn.enabled.markdownDescription: Incrementally correlate Claude Code and Codex shell history on startup, on transcript changes, and during periodic reconciliation. Confirmed successes add evidence, failures are retained as negative evidence, and unanswered calls are ignored. Raw transcript arguments and absolute transcript paths are never saved in Auto Learn state.

enumDescriptions: Learn counts only; never propose or apply policy.
Learn continuously and show candidates for review (recommended).
Automatically apply only deterministic, suffix-closed read-only candidates after the success threshold and with zero confirmed failures.
permissionWildcarding.autoLearn.mode.markdownDescription: Auto Learn operating mode. `auto-safe` requires a suffix-closed read-only prefix, judged on the *pattern* rather than the observed command: an applied `Bash(<root> *)` also matches `<root> ... > <path>`, and no allow pattern can exclude a redirection. Auto-safe is therefore limited to roots where no argument can reach stdout — `echo`, `printf`, `Write-*`, `basename`, `dirname`, `Get-Date` and `git cat-file` are excluded, along with destructive, administrative, credential-related, network-capable, package-install, wrapper, and ambiguous candidates. All remain review-only. Accepted residual: an auto-safe root can still truncate a path with fixed content (`whoami > f`), so keep catastrophic paths in `permissions.deny`.

permissionWildcarding.autoLearn.successT.markdownDescription: Successful correlated executions required before a normalized command family becomes eligible for automatic safe application.

permissionWildcarding.autoLearn.interval.markdownDescription: Periodic reconciliation interval in minutes. File watchers usually learn sooner; reconciliation catches events missed while VS Code was suspended.

permissionWildcarding.autoLearn.debounce.markdownDescription: How long to wait after transcript activity settles before a watcher-driven scan runs, in seconds. Higher = fewer scans during active work (the periodic reconcile is the backstop). Auto Learn reads incrementally, so a later scan just processes a larger batch — nothing is lost.

enumDescriptions: Write the dedicated user rule file at `~/.codex/rules/permission-wildcarding.rules`.
Learn from Codex history but do not write Codex rules.
permissionWildcarding.autoLearn.codexSco.markdownDescription:
Where validated generated Codex rules are written. Codex loads rules at startup, so restart Codex after a rule change.

`workspace` is **withdrawn**: its trust model could not be stated, because VS Code workspace trust, this setting and Codex's own project trust are three different decisions and only the last governs whether Codex loads a workspace rule file. A settings file that still says `workspace` is accepted, but Codex rule export stays OFF and the Auto Learn card says so. To remove rules an older release wrote into a repository: `wildcard-perms --codex-workspace-rules remove`.

permissionWildcarding.autoLearn.codexExe.markdownDescription: Command name or absolute path used for `codex execpolicy check`. Auto Learn never writes a Codex rule unless this validation succeeds.

permissionWildcarding.localDrain.enabled.markdownDescription: Promote portable approvals from each workspace's `.claude/settings.local.json` — the file Claude Code writes an "always approve" into — up to user-scope `settings.json`, then drop the local entries user scope now covers. Only clean command families move (`Bash(<root> *)`, `Tool(<root> <sub> *)`); script blobs, absolute-path executables, MCP tools and file/web families stay local. A local entry is removed only after its promotion is verified in `settings.json`, so a pruned entry is always still granted. Refused while legacy blanket `Bash(*)` and `PowerShell(*)` grants remain, because they cover every local entry. Untrusted workspaces are read-only.

permissionWildcarding.guidance.enabled.markdownDescription: Maintain a short managed block in each installed agent’s user-scope instruction file (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, and `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` when Codex is installed) telling the agent to write one command per tool call. An approval is stored as the command *string*: a single command becomes a reusable wildcard, while a compound command (`cd x && build`, multi-statement PowerShell) is stored verbatim and never matches again — the friction no generalizer can fix after the fact. Codex needs it for a different reason: its policy is an argv prefix for the program actually executed, so a `bash -lc` wrapper around `cd x && build` is a `bash` invocation that no rule for the real tool can match. Marker-fenced, so turning it off removes exactly what was added.

permissionWildcarding.gates.enabled.markdownDescription: Maintain a second managed block holding your own **standing orders**, compiled out of your Claude Code file-memory. `recall.py --gates-compile` lifts the `<!-- gate -->` section from every memory marked `scope: global` into `~/.claude/gates.generated.md`, and this installs it into each agent's instruction file. Why it needs to be resident: the memory index is a list of one-line hooks, so the enforceable half of a rule sits in a file that only loads if a recall surfaces it — which never happens for a rule you are already breaking, because nothing triggers the lookup. Reference material is fine on demand; policy is not. Installing is a file read and runs on activation; compiling spawns python and stays an explicit action. Marker-fenced separately from the shell-style block, so turning either off leaves the other byte-identical.

permissionWildcarding.memory.enabled.markdownDescription: Lint the Claude Code file-memory index (`MEMORY.md`) for bloat and broken links: a status-bar gauge plus editor diagnostics on over-budget hook lines and links to missing files.

permissionWildcarding.memory.dir.markdownDescription: Absolute path to a specific memory dir to lint (the folder containing `MEMORY.md`). Leave empty to auto-discover every `~/.claude/projects/*/memory/MEMORY.md`.

permissionWildcarding.memory.lineBudget.markdownDescription: Max **characters in one** `MEMORY.md` index line before it's flagged. (This is a width limit for a single hook, not a limit on how many lines the file may have — that's `#permissionWildcarding.memory.maxLines#`.) Hooks over this are drifting into changelog territory — move the detail into the memory file or the project repo.

permissionWildcarding.memory.maxLines.markdownDescription: How many **lines** of `MEMORY.md` Claude Code actually loads. It reads the first 200 lines (or 25 KB, whichever comes first) and drops the rest **without reporting it**, so anything past the cap is silently absent from every session. This is the limit that usually arrives first, because the index grows by roughly a line per project while its byte count barely moves. Change it only if the loader's cap changes.

permissionWildcarding.memory.totalBudget.markdownDescription: Byte budget for the whole always-loaded `MEMORY.md` index before the gauge warns.

permissionWildcarding.memory.recallScrip.markdownDescription: Absolute path to your permission-wildcarding repo's `memory/recall.py`. Enables the dashboard Memory card's **Rebuild recall index** button (a CPU bge-small re-embed of the memory dir). Leave empty to auto-detect the repo layout; the passive CPU-LLM status probe works either way.
